title: Strict split compact-flat-generator resolution of a bounded tower
statement: Let $Y$ be any scheme and $A$ its category of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $E_n$ be cochain complexes of $A$, with maps $t_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$, and suppose each $E_n$ is zero in degrees above some integer (no common upper bound is assumed). There are complexes $L_n$, maps $l_n:L_n\to L_{n+1}$ and quasi-isomorphisms $v_n:L_n\to E_n$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], with $l_nv_{n+1}=v_nt_n$. Each $L_n$ is bounded above and every $l_n^i$ admits a retraction. For each $(n,i)$ there is a set $I$ in the scheme's universe and flat module sheaves $G_j$, $j\in I$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], with $L_n^i\cong\bigoplus_{j\in I}G_j$. Each $G_j$ is compact for coproducts in the following explicit sense: for every set $K$ in that universe, family $H_k$ of module sheaves, and morphism $f:G_j\to\bigoplus_{k\in K}H_k$, there are a finite subset $S\subset K$ and a morphism $g:G_j\to\bigoplus_{k\in S}H_k$ such that $g$ followed by the canonical subcoproduct inclusion is $f$.

source.place: Original proof, first paragraph: relative generator resolution using 03EW, 077J and the cone induction of 06XX.

proof.text: The explicit zero complex is bounded above and has an empty coproduct decomposition in every degree. The empty coproduct is zero by Sigma.hom_ext, and its generator flatness and finite-support conditions are vacuous. Apply the finite relative-extension theorem to its zero map into E_0 to obtain the initial bounded generator resolution.

Package a stage n as a complex L_n and a quasi-isomorphism v_n into E_n, together with its upper bound and generator property. For each packaged stage apply the relative-extension theorem to v_n followed by t_n. This supplies a packaged successor and a degreewise split transition commuting strictly with the comparison maps. Choose these successor functions and transitions within the existential proof.

Use dependent Nat.rec from the initial packaged stage and the chosen successor. Define the requested L, l and v by projections of this recursion; the recursion equation makes the successor types agree definitionally. Project the bound, quasi-isomorphism, strict commutation, splitting, and generator witnesses to obtain each clause of the original conclusion. All choices occur inside this proof; no definition extracts arbitrary data from an unproved existence statement.

proof_origin.place: Dependent recursion formalizing the original relative cone induction; its one finite extension is separated into lem-sc-compact-flat-generator-relative-extension.

theorem exists_compact_flat_generator_tower_resolution (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (E : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (t : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1))
    (hb : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero ((E n).X i)) :
    ∃ (L : ℕ → CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
      (l : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⟶ L (n + 1)) (v : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⟶ E n),
      (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero ((L n).X i)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (v n)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, l n ≫ v (n + 1) = v n ≫ t n) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), IsSplitMono ((l n).f i)) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), ∃ (I : Type u)
        (G : I → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)),
        Nonempty ((L n).X i ≅ ∐ G) ∧
        (∀ j : I, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (G j)) ∧
        ∀ (j : I) (K : Type u)
          (H : K → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
          (f : G j ⟶ ∐ H),
          ∃ (S : Finset K) (g : G j ⟶ ∐ (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ H k.1)),
            g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ Sigma.ι H k.1) = f
